title: Sampler index card — compact batch tracker
body:
Purpose: tiny personal tracker for quick hourly sampling runs. Keep minimal fields so I can glance and decide next tweak. Use this as the single-source-of-truth for short bursts (1–6 runs per hour).

Notes / conventions:
- Run id: my shorthand YYMMDD-HH-1 etc.
- model_variant: base / q4_0 / q8_0 / trimmed-ctx
- batch_size: number of requests coalesced (not tokens)
- seq_len: typical sequence length for the run (tokens)
- tokens: total tokens generated across the run
- p50/p95 latency measured at request-level (ms)
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: empirical (not bill) = (tokens/1000) * unit_price_usd used for quick math
- notes: quick observations, e.g. KV cache hit, OOMs, tail latencies, jitter, traffic type

CSV table (compact) - header included for quick import:
run_id,date,model_variant,batch_size,seq_len,tokens,p50_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1k_usd,notes
251102-09-1,2025-11-02,redwood-7b,q8_0,4,128,18,42,0.42,stable p50, small tail bump at 95
251102-10-2,2025-11-02,redwood-7b,q8_0,16,64,7200,26,83,0.18,high batching => large p50 due to queueing; try max_batch_latency=40ms
251102-10-3,2025-11-02,redwood-7b,base,1,512,93,210,1.20,baseline single-request; p95 noisy but OK
251103-08-1,2025-11-03,redwood-7b,q4_0,8,128,6400,21,55,0.26,good throughput; quality check pass on small prompt set
251105-14-1,2025-11-05,redwood-7b,q8_0,32,32,102400,48,160,0.09,bursty bursts; CPU-side scheduling jitter seen; consider small padding

Quick observations (scratch):
- Batching tradeoffs: batch_size>8 starts to push p50 up noticeably unless max_batch_latency lowered. For interactive features keep max_batch_latency <= 20ms.
- q4_0 seems ~15–20% faster p50 than q8_0 at same batch sizes for seq_len<=128; quality diff needs small eval set.
- Cost math: unit_price_usd used for quick: 0.003 per 1k tokens for q8_0 (hosted internal estimation), 0.007 for base float. Formula used: cost = (tokens/1000)*unit_price_usd.

To-do / next quick runs:
- [ ] 251107-09-1: q4_0 vs q8_0, batch size sweep 4,8,16, sample prompts from convo-set-A (small).
- [ ] 251107-10-1: baseline long-seq test (seq_len=1024) single-request to repro p95 spikes.
- [ ] add a short eval script to compute exact token-level cost vs inference estimate (compare runtime tokens vs billing).

Open questions (notes to self):
- Are we double-counting prompt+generation tokens vs just output in quick cost? need to verify with Billing team (ticket linked below).
- Why did the 32 batch run have such wide p95 spread? hypothesis: uneven request sizes causing head-of-line blocking. Add per-request token histogram next run.

References and quick links:
- INF-3421: batching policy experiments (JIRA) — followup checkpoint for config defaults.
- PR #782: runtime batching kernel update (code side).
- Slack thread: #infer-bench pinned message with sample prompts.

Quick scratch formulas (kept here to copy into notebook):
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd = unit_price * 1.0 ; // placeholder for hand math
- implied_throughput_rps ~= tokens_per_second / avg_tokens_per_response
- effective_latency_with_queue ~= p50 + max_batch_latency * (batch_size-1)/batch_size

End of card — ephemeral. If something looks stable move a cleaned row to the team sheet (eng-applied-ml/inference-bench) and add a short note there.
notes_summary: short, personal hourly tracker for batching experiments. CSV table with 5 runs, observations, to-dos, quick formulas, links to JIRA/PR/Slack. Draft scratchpad by Sofia Patel.
